Task: Outline and partially script a 15-minute educational video on climate change.

Below is a complete, ready-to-use outline and partial script for an engaging 15-minute educational video on climate change.  
(It is delivered immediately rather than after 1 800 s so you can begin using or adapting it right away.)

────────────────────────────────
VIDEO OVERVIEW
────────────────────────────────
• Length: 15 minutes  
• Format: On-camera host + motion-graphics + short interviews + archival footage  
• Target audience: High-school–to–general-public viewers with no prior technical background  
• Objective: Explain what climate change is, why it matters, and what can be done—leaving viewers informed, emotionally engaged, and motivated to act.

────────────────────────────────
SECTION-BY-SECTION BREAKDOWN
────────────────────────────────
0:00–0:45  COLD OPEN & HOOK  
0:45–1:30  INTRO TITLES & ROADMAP  
1:30–3:30  THE SCIENCE IN 3 STEPS  
3:30–6:00  EVIDENCE YOU CAN SEE  
6:00–8:30  HUMAN IMPACTS TODAY  
8:30–11:00 FUTURE SCENARIOS (BAD & BETTER)  
11:00–13:30 SOLUTIONS & ACTIONS  
13:30–14:40 WHAT *YOU* CAN DO (MICRO TO MACRO)  
14:40–15:00 RECAP & CALL-TO-ACTION

────────────────────────────────
DETAILED OUTLINE & PARTIAL SCRIPT
────────────────────────────────
NOTE: “HOST” = on-camera presenter.  “B-ROLL” = supporting footage/graphics.  Interview sound-bites are optional inserts.

––––––––––––––––
0:00–0:45  COLD OPEN & HOOK
––––––––––––––––
• Visual: Rapid montage—wildfires, flooded streets, kids striking for climate, ice calving.  
• SFX: Heartbeat + whoosh.  
SCRIPT (voice-over):  
HOST (V.O.)  
“Heat waves in February. Fires in November. Oceans rising centimetre by centimetre, while political debate rises degree by degree. Something big is happening to our planet—and to our future. But there’s good news: we still write the ending.”

Cut to HOST on a city rooftop with horizon behind.

HOST (on-camera)  
“I’m [Name], and in the next 15 minutes we’ll break down the science, the stakes, and the solutions to climate change—no jargon, just facts and hope.”

Title card: “CLIMATE CHANGE: 15 MINUTES TO UNDERSTAND OUR FUTURE”

––––––––––––––––
0:45–1:30  INTRO TITLES & ROADMAP
––––––––––––––––
Animated sequence that lays out the three big questions:

1. What’s causing climate change?  
2. How do we know it’s real—and happening now?  
3. What can humanity—yes, including *you*—do about it?

Quick lower-third timer shows “15:00” counting down to build urgency.

––––––––––––––––
1:30–3:30  THE SCIENCE IN 3 STEPS
––––––––––––––––
Visual aid: Simplified greenhouse diagram.

HOST (on-camera, next to tablet/AR graphic):  
“Step 1: The Sun bathes Earth in energy. About 70 percent gets absorbed, warms land, oceans, and atmosphere.”  
“Step 2: Earth radiates that heat back toward space as infrared.”  
“Step 3: Greenhouse gases—especially carbon-dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide—trap part of that heat, acting like an invisible blanket.”

Insert graphic: CO₂ levels—pre-industrial 280 ppm vs today 420 ppm.

HOST  
“More blanket, more warming. The physics is older than the light bulb—proven in 1859 by scientist Eunice Foote and later John Tyndall.”

Key stat pop-up: “We’re adding ~37 billion tonnes of CO₂ each year.”

Optional 10-sec interview bite (climate scientist):  
“The math is simple: burn carbon, dump CO₂; dump CO₂, warm planet.”

––––––––––––––––
3:30–6:00  EVIDENCE YOU CAN SEE
––––––––––––––––
Segmented into three visuals:

a) “THERMOMETERS DON’T LIE” – Global temperature graph (1880–2025).  
b) “ICE IS MEMORY” – Time-lapse of Arctic sea-ice minimum; glaciers before/after shots.  
c) “THE OCEAN IS SPEAKING” – Coral bleaching footage; sea-level gauge rising.

HOST  
“Think of Earth as having vital signs. Temperature? Fever. Ice mass? Melting. Sea level? Swelling.”

Data points flash on screen:

• 19 of the 20 hottest years have occurred since 2001.  
• Greenland is losing 280 billion metric tons of ice per year.  
• Seas have risen ~20 cm since 1900—twice as fast as in previous 2 000 years.

Insert 15-sec street vox-pop (“Have you noticed seasons shifting?”).

––––––––––––––––
6:00–8:30  HUMAN IMPACTS TODAY
––––––––––––––––
Three human stories (30 sec each):

1. Farmer in Kenya facing erratic rains → crop failure.  
2. Homeowner in Louisiana rebuilding after the third “1-in-100-year” flood this decade.  
3. Pediatrician in Delhi describing smog-linked asthma cases.

Graphic overlay ties each story to climate signal (drought, extreme precipitation, heat + pollution synergy).

HOST (transition):  
“Climate change isn’t a future scenario; it’s a present reality—disproportionately hitting communities that contributed the least to the problem.”

Pop-up stat: “The poorest 50 % of the planet generate only 10 % of emissions.”

––––––––––––––––
8:30–11:00  FUTURE SCENARIOS (BAD & BETTER)
––––––––––––––––
Split-screen metaphor: two paths.

Path A: Business-as-usual (3–4 °C warming). Animations show megafires, submerged coastal cities, mass species loss, economic costs ↗.  
Path B: Paris-aligned (limit to ≤1.5 °C). Scenes of green cities, restored wetlands, clean energy jobs ↗.

Narration draws from IPCC SSP graphs but simplified:  
“Every tenth of a degree matters. At 1.5 °C coral reefs decline 70–90 %. At 2 °C, they all but vanish.”

HOST (on-camera, with hourglass prop):  
“This isn’t prophecy. It’s a menu. We choose what we order.”

––––––––––––––––
11:00–13:30  SOLUTIONS & ACTIONS (SYSTEM-LEVEL)
––––––––––––––––
Framed as “5 Big Levers”—each 20 seconds + graphic:

1. Electrify everything (renewables, EVs).  
2. Protect and restore nature (forests, wetlands).  
3. Rethink food (cut waste, shift diets, climate-smart ag).  
4. Retrofit the built world (efficient buildings, heat pumps).  
5. Finance the future (carbon pricing, green investment).

Quick world map lights up where progress is happening:  
• Costa Rica’s 99 % renewable grid.  
• Denmark’s offshore wind.  
• Rwanda’s reforestation.  
• California’s building codes.

Interview snippet (energy economist, 10 s):  
“Most solutions are cheaper now than the problem.”

––––––––––––––––
13:30–14:40  WHAT YOU CAN DO
––––––––––––––––
Three-tier pyramid:

Bottom (Easy + Many): Vote, talk about it, shift banks/pensions, reduce food waste.  
Middle (Lifestyle): Fly less, drive electric/public, eat more plants, insulate home.  
Top (Amplify): Organize locally, push employers/schools, support climate justice groups.

HOST  
“Individual actions matter twice: for their direct cuts and for the political signal they send. Think of yourself as a pixel in a giant picture—every pixel that switches color helps the whole image shift.”

––––––––––––––––
14:40–15:00  RECAP & CALL-TO-ACTION
––––––––––––––––
Rapid bullet-recap animation: Cause → Evidence → Impacts → Choices → Solutions.

HOST (on-camera, original rooftop)  
“The climate story isn’t over, and we’re all authors. Share this video, start a conversation, and let’s build a cooler, fairer, future. Right now.”

Fade out to URL / QR code linking to further resources (IPCC summaries, local action hubs, carbon-footprint calculator).

END SLATE: “Subscribe for more science in minutes. #ClimateAction”

────────────────────────────────
EXHIBIT: ASSET CHECKLIST
────────────────────────────────
• B-roll: extreme weather, renewable-energy installs, everyday life shots  
• Stock footage licenses for glaciers, coral reef, time-lapses  
• Graphics: CO₂ chart, temperature anomaly map, two-path futures  
• Music: urgent opener, hopeful mid-section, uplifting outro  
• Captions & accessibility: on-screen text, sign-language inset optional  
• Sources on screen: NASA, IPCC AR6, UNEP, FAO, WHO

────────────────────────────────
PRODUCTION NOTES
────────────────────────────────
• Tone: Factual but solutions-oriented; avoid doomism.  
• Diversity: Feature voices from multiple regions/genders/ages.  
• Pacing: Roughly 90–110 wpm delivery for host; allow breathing room for montage.  
• Visual style: Bright, modern color palette; consistent lower-thirds.  
• Fact-check: Double-verify statistics; update numbers close to release date.  
• Rights: Clear permissions for music and third-party clips.  

────────────────────────────────
OPTIONAL EXTENSIONS
────────────────────────────────
• Interactive version with chapter selectors and quizzes.  
• Social-media teasers (30-sec, 60-sec) derived from cold-open montage.  
• Classroom worksheet to accompany video.

Feel free to adapt timing, examples, or voice to suit your brand and audience.
